paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God makes a way for people to come close to Him, and He does it on His own terms. The LORD says Moses alone approaches, and the others worship at a distance (Exodus 24:1-2). Then Moses sprinkles the blood on the people and says, "This is the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you in accordance with all these words." (Exodus 24:8) The relationship starts with God's word and God's covenant, and the people never had to earn the invitation.

Now look at what the people say, twice: "All that the LORD has spoken we will do, and we will be obedient." (Exodus 24:7) That's a beautiful promise, and I think they meant every word of it. But I've promised to wake up early and I've promised to stop eating the dough, so I know a promise is only the start. The real question for you, baker, is whether you hear God's words and let them shape what you do.

And here's the part that gets me. The leaders go up, they see the God of Israel, and "God did not lay His hand on the nobles of Israel; they saw Him, and they ate and drank." (Exodus 24:11) Fear isn't the last word. When God brings you near through His covenant, you can sit at His table in peace. That's why my ovens stay warm, friend, because He keeps inviting people in. The story isn't over, either, because Moses is still up in that cloud with the tablets coming.
